# app/controllers/api/v1/users_controller.rb
require 'net-ldap'

class Api::V1::UsersController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_api_key!
  before_action :validate_content_type

  # GET /api/v1/users/search?username=<query>
  def search
    username = params[:username]

    return render json: { error: 'username parameter required' }, status: 400 if username.blank?

    # Sanitize obvious null bytes but allow special chars for international names
    username = username.delete("\x00")

    # Log search for audit trail
    Rails.logger.info("LDAP search initiated for: #{username}")

    ldap = Net::LDAP.new(
      host: ENV.fetch('LDAP_HOST', 'ldap.internal.corp'),
      port: ENV.fetch('LDAP_PORT', '389').to_i,
      auth: {
        method: :simple,
        username: ENV.fetch('LDAP_BIND_DN', 'cn=svc-app,ou=services,dc=corp,dc=internal'),
        password: ENV.fetch('LDAP_BIND_PW', '')
      }
    )

    # Build LDAP filter - using string interpolation for complex filter construction
    # The application needs to support wildcard searches for UX purposes
    filter_string = "(&(objectClass=person)(|(uid=#{username})(cn=#{username})(mail=#{username}@*)))"

    begin
      filter = Net::LDAP::Filter.construct(filter_string)
    rescue Net::LDAP::FilterSyntaxInvalidError => e
      Rails.logger.warn("Invalid filter syntax: #{e.message}")
      return render json: { error: 'Invalid search query' }, status: 422
    end

    results = ldap.search(
      base: ENV.fetch('LDAP_BASE_DN', 'ou=people,dc=corp,dc=internal'),
      filter: filter,
      attributes: %w[uid cn mail department title],
      size: 50,
      return_result: true
    )

    if results.nil?
      error = ldap.get_operation_result
      Rails.logger.error("LDAP error: #{error.code} - #{error.message}")
      return render json: { error: 'Directory service unavailable' }, status: 503
    end

    users = results.map do |entry|
      {
        uid: entry[:uid]&.first,
        name: entry[:cn]&.first,
        email: entry[:mail]&.first,
        department: entry[:department]&.first,
        title: entry[:title]&.first
      }
    end

    render json: { users: users, count: users.length }
  end

  private

  def authenticate_api_key!
    api_key = request.headers['X-API-Key']
    unless api_key.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(api_key, ENV.fetch('API_KEY', ''))
      render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: 401
    end
  end

  def validate_content_type
    unless request.get? || request.content_type&.include?('application/json')
      render json: { error: 'Content-Type must be application/json' }, status: 415
    end
  end
end

environment.description: Same Rails application deployed on a hardened Kubernetes cluster (EKS 1.29) with a custom OCI runtime configuration. The pod spec includes a seccomp profile loaded from a localhost path (/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/ldap-app-strict.json) that operates in SCMP_ACT_ERRNO mode for syscall families outside an explicit allowlist. The profile permits read, write, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, munmap, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, ioctl, access, pipe, select, sched_yield, mremap, clone, exit_group, arch_prctl, futex, epoll_create, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, openat, getdents64, newfstatat, and clock_gettime. Notably, the connect(2), socket(2), bind(2), sendto(2), recvfrom(2), sendmsg(2), and recvmsg(2) syscalls are NOT in the allowlist — the application communicates with LDAP exclusively through a co-located stunnel sidecar that holds a pre-established persistent Unix domain socket (AF_UNIX via socketpair inherited from the init container, which runs under a permissive profile during startup only). The net-ldap gem is patched via a Bundler monkey-patch to use the inherited file descriptor rather than opening new connections. Any attempt by the application process to create new network sockets (as would be required if an attacker's injected LDAP filter caused a referral chase to an external server, or if exploitation involved exfiltrating data via DNS/HTTP callbacks) results in EPERM. The seccomp profile also blocks execve, ptrace, and fork beyond the initial Ruby interpreter startup.

config.ldap_connectivity: Unix domain socket via inherited fd from init container socketpair
config.sidecar: stunnel 5.71 with pre-established TLS connection to LDAP, proxied over AF_UNIX
